_nota: Summary of the INIFAP 2026 Agricultural Technical Agenda, built from the text in data/inifap/extraido/baja_california_sur.json following pipeline/inifap/instrucciones_resumen.md. No pesticide brands or doses.
fuente: INIFAP. Agenda Técnica Agrícola de Baja California Sur [Agricultural Technical Agenda of Baja California Sur]. INIFAP, Mexico City, 2026.

fichas.region: Semi-warm arid subtropical climate. Regosol, yermosol and vertisol soils; in the farming areas almost all are alkaline (average pH 8.41) with medium to sandy loam texture.

siembra.texto: In the Valle de Santo Domingo it yields well from October 1 to the second half of December, but the optimal period is November 25 to December 31. October plantings suffer more pests because of the heat; October and November plantings risk frost during pod filling; January plantings, more foliar diseases and pests.

fichas.densidad: 12 seeds per linear meter, about 5 cm deep. Rows 80 cm apart with a single line, or 1.60 m beds with double lines 40 cm apart.
fichas.fertilizacion: Formula 90-40-00 with UAN 32 and phosphoric acid. The N is split into three applications at 10, 35 and 60 days after sowing; all the P at 10 days. Foliar applications of iron chelates to prevent or correct deficiencies.
fichas.riego: Furrow (gravity): an initial flood irrigation and two to three supplemental irrigations starting at flowering, in furrows shorter than 100 m. Drip: dry planting and weekly irrigations of about seven hours. Center pivot: wet the soil for planting and three to five supplemental irrigations of three to five days each.
plagas: Pod borer (Chloridea virescens and Helicoverpa zea)
fichas.malezas: Main weeds: yellow flower (Aldama dentata), morning glory (Ipomoea purpurea) and quelite (Amaranthus hybridus). Controlled with one pre-emergence herbicide application.
fichas.cosecha: Cut when the plant is dry but the grain is still soft, and let it dry in the field down to 12 % moisture. The suggested varieties exceed 3 t/ha with the technology package.
cuidados: Plant from November 25 to December 31 to reduce damage from pests, frost and diseases.
Inoculate the seed with Mesorhizobium ciceri in the shade, following the manufacturer, and plant it the same day.
Plow only if the land is very compacted or there are many rodents.
Apply pest control only when the threshold is reached: 20 % of foliage damaged with live leafminer larvae, or two or more pod borer larvae per linear meter.
Prevent diseases with tolerant varieties, crop rotation, the recommended planting date and quality seed.
Split the nitrogen into three applications (10, 35 and 60 days after sowing).
fichas.nota: Costs from Table 2 (FIRA 2026), with drip irrigation. The total cost of 51,685 $/ha matches the sum of the items and gross income is 3.0 t × 20,625 $/t = 61,875 $/ha (the table calls it 'Beneficio ha'). The table prints a B/C ratio of 1.22 and a cost per ton of 16,856 $, which correspond to a cost of about 50,568 $/ha and do not match the total; here net income (61,875 − 51,685) and B/C ratio (61,875 / 51,685 ≈ 1.20) were calculated. The price is per ton.

fichas.region: Fall-winter Desi-type chickpea, 110 to 140 days. Adapts from sea level to 1,800 m; ideal temperature 18 to 26 °C and low relative humidity. Hard frosts at flowering damage it. Rainfed it needs 400 to 650 mm well distributed, although it produces acceptable forage with residual soil moisture.

siembra.texto: The ideal planting runs from November 15 to December 15. In the Valle de Santo Domingo it yields well from October 15 to January 15, and plantings from November 25 to December 31 give the highest yield. October plantings give more forage and crop residues than January ones.

fichas.densidad: 10 seeds per linear meter (27 kg of pure live seed per ha), 5 cm deep, in single-line rows 80 cm apart.
fichas.fertilizacion: Base nutrition on a soil analysis. Formula 120-70-00: the N in three equal parts at 15, 30 and 50 days after sowing, and all the P at 15 days.
fichas.riego: Furrow (gravity): a flood irrigation, one supplemental irrigation before flowering and two more after, in furrows shorter than 100 m. Drip on clay soils: dry planting and weekly irrigations of about seven hours (6-mil tape, emitters every 20 cm). Center pivot: wet the soil for planting and three to four supplemental irrigations.
fichas.malezas: Weed competition in the first 40 days greatly reduces grain and straw yield. Pre-emergence control activated with the irrigation water is recommended.
fichas.cosecha: For forage at flowering, cut at about 70 days; at pod formation, at about 100 days; at maturity, when the plant is dry and the grain soft, and dry down to 10 to 12 % moisture (130 to 140 days). Older plants give more forage but lower quality. Under optimal conditions it produces 8 to 12 t/ha of dry forage and 2.5 to 3.5 t/ha of grain.
cuidados: Keep the crop free of weeds during the first 40 days.
Use varieties tolerant to chickpea wilt, rotate crops, plant on time and use good-quality seed.
Monitor pests when the cold season ends: without control they can cut grain by 5 to 10 %.
Choose the cutting stage according to forage needs: later cutting gives more volume but lower quality.
Subsoil or plow only on compacted land or land with many soil pests.
fichas.nota: The sheet covers irrigated and rainfed (modalidad null); Table 3 (FIRA 2026) is for furrow (gravity) irrigation with pre-planting irrigation and 3 supplemental irrigations. The table's yield is seed (grain), not forage. The price (19.5 $/kg) is not printed: it was calculated as gross income / yield (48,750 / 2,500). Total cost, net income and B/C ratio match. The text gives two planting windows (Nov 15–Dec 15 as ideal and Nov 25–Dec 31 as highest yielding). Diseases: the text names none in that section; it only mentions the varieties' tolerance to chickpea wilt.

fichas.region: Semi-warm arid subtropics, mean temperature of 22.1 °C and annual rainfall of 172 mm. Sandy loam eutric regosol soil, 20 to 100 cm deep, with 0.6 % organic matter and pH 8.2. 90 % of the maize is planted in Comondú.

siembra.texto: From February 5 to March 20 in spring-summer and from August 15 to September 15 in fall-winter.

fichas.densidad: Six to seven plants per linear meter (75 to 87 thousand plants/ha; some materials tolerate 100 thousand), with 18 to 20 kg of seed. Rows 75–80 cm apart and 14 to 16 cm between plants; with drip, 1.6 m beds with double lines 40 cm apart. Depth of 5 to 8 cm.
fichas.fertilizacion: Up to 200-80-100 per ha, although there is good response with 180 of N and 40 to 60 of P, useful to lower costs. Split the nitrogen.
fichas.riego: Needs 500 to 550 mm. Early materials: four irrigations at 0, 45, 65 and 85 days (18, 12, 12 and 12 cm). Intermediate and late materials: five irrigations (18, 12, 10, 10 and 10 cm). Critical stages: development, stem elongation, flowering and milk-dough grain. Gravity in 100 m furrows; sprinkler with a 16 cm pre-planting irrigation and 8 cm supplemental irrigations; drip with an initial irrigation of about 16 h and about 25 supplemental irrigations of 5 to 7 h.
fichas.malezas: Choose land free of morning glory and use well-rotted manure. Plant into moist soil with certified seed. Do mechanical cultivations between 30 and 35 days after sowing and hand weeding. Near harvest, weed or slash so weeds do not shed seed, or control right after harvest.
fichas.cosecha: Harvest at 16 to 18 % grain moisture: drier reduces yield and wetter causes storage losses. Diatomaceous earth reduces storage pests. Expected yield: 10 t/ha.
cuidados: Avoid sandy land coming from sorghum, wheat, maize or chickpea with heavy lesser cornstalk borer or cutworm pressure.
Control fall armyworm only if there is 10 % damage in plants shorter than 20 cm or 20 % in plants 20 to 40 cm tall.
Release Trichogramma wasps (100 to 150 thousand per ha, twice a week) from flowering to dough grain against corn earworm.
Protect beneficial insects (lady beetles, lacewings, wasps and bees).
Ensure water during flowering and grain filling.
Harvest with grain moisture between 16 and 18 %.
fichas.nota: Planted in two cycles (PV and OI), hence ciclo null. The text does not state the origin or company of the suggested genotypes; they are listed as they appear and public varieties were not separated. Costs from Table 4 (FIRA 2025): the total cost of 43,500 $/ha matches the sum of the items and gross income is 10,000 kg × 6 $/kg = 60,000 $. The table prints net income of 20,100 and B/C ratio of 1.50, calculated with a cost of 39,900 $ that does not match the total; here they were calculated with 43,500 $ (net 16,500; B/C ≈ 1.38). The table's water fee (5 × 500) appears as 2,250 instead of 2,500.

fichas.region: Very dry climate in almost the whole state, mean temperature of 18 to 22 °C and less than 200 mm of rain per year, concentrated from July to September; that is why it is grown only under irrigation. Optimal temperature range of 18 to 33 °C; needs more than 10 °C to germinate.

siembra.texto: From February 5 to March 20 in spring-summer and from August 15 to September 15 in fall-winter.

fichas.densidad: Seven to eight plants per meter of row (87,500 to 100,000 plants/ha) in a single line; with drip, 1.6 m beds with double lines 0.4 m apart and 14 to 16 plants per meter of bed. 20 to 23 kg of seed per ha.
fichas.fertilizacion: Formula 180-60-00. With surface irrigation, all the P and 40 % of the N at planting and the remaining 60 % of N at the cultivation pass. With pressurized irrigation, N by stages: 15 % at planting (0–30 days), 40 % during growth (30–50), 30 % at flowering-silking (50–75) and 15 % at grain filling (75–100).
fichas.riego: Water use of 500 to 660 mm. Gravity: early materials with a flood irrigation (18 cm) and supplemental irrigations at 40–45, 65–70 and 85–90 days (12 cm); intermediate and late materials with supplemental irrigations at 40–45, 60–65, 80–85 and 100–105 days (12 cm). Sprinkler: 160 mm pre-planting irrigation and 80 mm supplemental irrigations (about 500 mm in total). Drip: about 450 mm with a germination irrigation and about 25 supplemental irrigations every three or four days. Critical stages: flowering, pollination, grain formation and grain filling.
enfermedades: Corn stunt (Spiroplasma kunkelii, transmitted by leafhoppers)
fichas.malezas: Choose land free of or lightly infested with morning glory and use certified seed free of other species. Do one or two mechanical cultivation passes between 30 and 40 days.
fichas.cosecha: Harvest when the grain milk line has advanced 30 to 50 %, the optimal point for green chopping or silage.
cuidados: Avoid sandy land coming from sorghum, wheat, maize or chickpea with heavy lesser cornstalk borer or cutworm pressure.
Use hybrids or varieties with pest resistance when possible.
Against stink bugs: monitoring, trap plants on the edges and conserving natural enemies.
Against common smut: do not exceed the recommended density and destroy the galls.
Against corn stunt: plant on time, use tolerant genotypes and monitor leafhoppers.
Harvest with the milk line between 30 and 50 %.
fichas.nota: Planted in two cycles (PV and OI), hence ciclo null. The text does not state the origin or company of the recommended materials; they are listed as they appear. Costs from Table 8 (based on FIRA Agrocostos): green forage yield. Total cost, gross income (48,850 $) and net income match. The price (977 $/t) is not printed: it was calculated as gross income / yield. The table prints a B/C ratio of 0.12, which is actually net income / cost (12.98 % return); here gross income / cost ≈ 1.13 was used.

fichas.region: Semi-warm arid subtropical climate. Regosol, yermosol and vertisol soils; in the farming areas almost all are alkaline (average pH 8.41) with medium to sandy loam texture. Tolerates drought, heat and salinity, and uses up to 30 % less water than maize.

siembra.texto: The best date in spring-summer is the second half of April, with drip irrigation in the Valle de Santo Domingo.

fichas.densidad: 16 to 18 kg of seed per ha depending on seed size, in rows 80 cm apart. Depth of 3 cm in dry planting and 5 cm in moist soil.
fichas.fertilizacion: Formula 100-60-00 with UAN 32 and phosphoric acid. The N in three equal parts at 10, 35 and 60 days after sowing; all the P at 10 days. Foliar applications of iron chelates.
fichas.riego: With drip: a 12-hour emergence irrigation and then weekly 7-hour irrigations.
fichas.malezas: One mechanical cultivation pass between 30 and 40 days after sowing. Main weeds: mallow, London rocket (Sisymbrium irio), purslane, quelite or pigweed, dock, yellow flower and morning glory.
fichas.cosecha: For silage, cut at milk-dough grain. For grazing, wait for at least 60 cm of height to avoid hydrocyanic acid or nitrate poisoning. Expected yield: about 63 t/ha of green forage.
cuidados: Plant in the second half of April.
Do not graze before the plant is 60 cm tall, to avoid livestock poisoning.
Conserve lady beetles, which naturally control the sugarcane aphid.
Watch for downy mildew, the main disease in the Valle de Santo Domingo; Gavatero 203 is susceptible.
Do one cultivation pass between 30 and 40 days to control weeds.
fichas.nota: The extracted data marked the crop type as 'anual/perenne'; the text says forage sorghum is an annual species. Costs from Table 10 (FIRA 2026), with drip irrigation: the total cost of 53,874 $/ha matches the sum of the items and gross income is 63 t × 1,200 $/t = 75,600 $ (the table calls it 'Beneficio ha'). The table prints a B/C ratio of 1.42 and a cost per ton of 842.33 $, which do not match the total; here net income (75,600 − 53,874) and B/C (≈ 1.40) were calculated.
